name: ARC (AI2 Reasoning Challenge)
description: The AI2 Reasoning Challenge (ARC) is a question set, text corpus, and baselines assembled to encourage AI research in advanced question answering. The ARC question set contains 7,787 natural, grade-school science questions (authored for human tests) and is partitioned into a Challenge Set (2,590 questions answered incorrectly by both a retrieval-based algorithm and a word co-occurrence algorithm) and an Easy Set (5,197 questions). The dataset also includes the ARC Corpus, a corpus of 14M science sentences relevant to the task.
creator: Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence (AI2)
citeAs: Clark, P., Cowhey, I., Etzioni, O., Khot, T., Sabharwal, A., Schoenick, C., & Tafjord, O. (2018). Think you have Solved Question Answering? Try ARC, the AI2 Reasoning Challenge. arXiv:1803.05457.
rai:dataCollection: Questions were collected through several months of extensive search and investigation, drawing from a variety of standardized test sources (grade-school science exams). The ARC Corpus was created by utilizing a major search engine to run a large series of search queries relevant to science. Queries were automatically constructed by instantiating approximately 100 hand-written templates for 80 science topics covered by US elementary and middle schools. The top several documents from each search were collected, de-duplicated, and stripped down to text, then chunked into sentences. The corpus was augmented with the AristoMini corpus containing dictionary definitions from Wiktionary, articles from Simple Wikipedia tagged as science, and additional science sentences collected from the Web.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Web API, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions were drawn from a variety of standardized test sources including ACTAAP, AIMS, Alaska Dept Ed, AMP, CA Standards Test, FCAT, LA Ed Assessment Program, Maryland School Assessment, MCAS, MEA, MEAP, Mercury (anonymous content partner of AI2), MSA, NAEP, NC READY, NY Regents, Ohio Achievement Tests, TAKS, TIMSS, VA Standards of Learning, and WASL. The ARC Corpus was sourced from web documents retrieved via a major search engine, augmented with the AristoMini corpus (Wiktionary definitions, Simple Wikipedia science articles, and additional web science sentences).
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions were partitioned into a Challenge Set and an Easy Set. The Challenge Set contains only questions answered incorrectly by both a retrieval-based (IR) algorithm and a word co-occurrence (PMI) algorithm. The IR solver uses the Waterloo corpus and Elasticsearch to find sentences supporting each answer option. The PMI solver uses pointwise mutual information over unigrams, bigrams, trigrams, and skipbigrams from the question and answer options. Questions answered correctly by either solver were placed in the Easy Set.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For the ARC Corpus: top documents from search queries were collected and de-duplicated, content was stripped to text only, and text was chunked into sentences. Approximately 75% of a random sample of 805 documents were judged as science relevant. For the entailment baseline models: questions were converted to Fill-In-The-Blank (FITB) statements by replacing wh-words with blanks, dropping phrases common in multiple-choice settings (e.g., 'of the following', 'of these'), and then filling in the blank with each answer choice to generate hypothesis sentences. Long sentences (>300 characters), sentences with negation, and noisy sentences were filtered from retrieved premises.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Elasticsearch (for IR-based retrieval and filtering), PMI solver using the Waterloo corpus, Open IE (for structured representation extraction in DGEM model), AllenNLP (framework for neural baseline models)
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The ARC Dataset, Corpus, three baseline neural models (DecompAttn, BiDAF, and DGEM), and a leaderboard are all available at http://data.allenai.org/arc. A leaderboard is maintained for up-to-date results.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to drive progress in AI research on advanced question answering, moving beyond factoid retrieval-style tasks toward questions requiring reasoning, commonsense knowledge, and deeper text comprehension. It is designed to encourage research on more difficult AI challenges rather than incremental improvements to simple algorithms.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset includes a publically releasable subset of the Kaggle Allen AI Science Challenge questions (about 60% of the Kaggle set, making up 43% of the ARC set). The Challenge Set definition is operationally defined by two specific baseline solvers (IR and PMI), meaning the partition approximates but does not perfectly capture the informal notion of 'hard' questions. Grade levels range from 3rd to 9th grade with substantial overlap in difficulty among grade levels.
rai:dataLimitations: The Challenge Set definition only approximates the informal goal of containing 'hard' questions, as it is defined by failure of two specific baseline algorithms. The ARC Corpus, while covering knowledge relevant to approximately 95% of Challenge questions, does not always contain direct answers, and simple retrieval methods are insufficient to exploit the distributed evidence. Only 11 question words (mainly proper nouns) do not appear in the corpus. The dataset contains only non-diagram, multiple-choice science questions for grades 3-9, limiting generalization to other question types or domains.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for use in training, development, and testing of question answering systems. It is specifically designed to benchmark advanced QA methods requiring reasoning, commonsense knowledge, and multi-hop inference, beyond simple retrieval or word co-occurrence methods. The ARC Corpus can optionally be used as a knowledge source for QA systems, though systems are not restricted to it.
